newsitem.title: UK: EU's internal sugar price seen pressured by policy.
newsitem.headline: EU's internal sugar price seen pressured by policy.

text.p: Market prices for sugar within the European Union (EU) will come under pressure from revisions to the trading bloc's centralised policy, especially if world prices continue to fall, a top EU official said on Thursday.
Ejner Stendevad, head of sugar in the EU's Directorate General for Agriculture, said a policy of low stocks had led to lower support prices, which should lead to lower market prices.
"The changes made last review will lead to increased pressure on prices, not in the short term but sooner than we believe if there is a fall in the world market price," he said.

Speaking at a two-day conference hosted by Agra Europe, Stendevad said the EU's sugar regime was reviewed in an unprecedented way in 1994/95 and the biggest challenge came from the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT).
The current regime will be valid until June 30, 2001, but could easily remain in place after that date and also withstand the EU's proposed eastward enlargement.
Due to a high degreee of security in supply, the EU was in a position to allow some of the lowest closing sugar stocks in the world, down to 30 days of consumption, he said.
"The only possibility to escape the impact of these changes is to have stable market prices, otherwise they (the changes) will have an impact," Stendevad said.
"We are not leaders of the world market, we are just partners there."
